title: Dedicated onboarding: Lighthouse setup visuals and capacity inspector
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Create a compact, scannable set of onboarding visuals and a midflow 'Capacity Inspector' canvas for Dedicated capacity setup. The goal is to reduce first-run confusion by exposing three contextual layers: recommended baseline (based on workload template), autoscale envelope (min/target/max), and SLA impact preview (99th pct latency vs cost). Deliverables: a hero quickstart graphic for the first-run modal, 3 size variants of the capacity inspector (compact, detail, fullscreen), a pair of micro-tiles for autoscale explainers, and a set of annotated screenshots for docs/release notes. Work must align with console tokens and be easy to convert into React components. Avoid reusing existing 'carousel' or 'storyboard' motifs; target a tool-like inspector metaphor with a left summary rail and right preview timeline.
acceptance_criteria: Figma file includes hero quickstart + three inspector states (compact/detail/fullscreen)
Annotated screenshots exported at 2x and 3x for documentation and marketing
Component spec pages with spacing tokens and copy-ready microcopy
PM/Eng sign-off that visuals map cleanly to Console components (cards, toggles, timelines)
Accessibility checks: color contrast >= 4.5:1 for key labels and keyboard-focus states documented
decisions: Use inspector metaphor instead of carousel to make state persistent when users navigate away
Expose autoscale as an envelope graphic (min/target/max) to communicate cost/latency tradeoffs visually
Default recommendation engine output will be shown as 'Suggested baseline' with a small confidence indicator
Avoid heavy animation in first-run modal to reduce cognitive load on low-spec devices
